title: Runtime output and character consistency hardening V1.1
description: Make CapCut visual media render-safe, add explicit MP4 download, lock character composition, and improve character-first recovery without changing legacy projects.
businessContext: Character-first projects can produce structurally valid output that is unreliable in CapCut, downloads without a usable MP4 filename, and do not constrain teacher framing consistently across generated shots.
dependencies: approved Character-first V1 domain and orchestration
acceptanceCriteria: CapCut receives validated H.264 visual clips with the project canvas, FPS, and shot duration instead of raw image files.
CapCut motion metadata maps to supported pycapcut animations without overwriting existing drafts.
Final Preview offers a typed Save As MP4 flow that always writes a playable .mp4 file after artifact and hash validation.
Character versions support an optional backward-compatible composition lock and prompts include the default half-body-right framing contract.
Character-first recovery binds an active approved version or exposes an actionable character checkpoint; legacy projects remain unchanged.
Shot Plan normalizes provider state metadata before schema validation and preserves safe needs_attention/retry behavior.
Focused tests, typecheck, and diff check pass.
verificationCommands: corepack pnpm exec vitest run packages/domain/test/character.test.ts packages/domain/test/ipcSchemas.test.ts packages/media/test/capcutVisual.test.ts apps/desktop/src/main/characterService.test.ts apps/desktop/src/main/shotPlanService.test.ts apps/desktop/src/main/capcutDraftService.test.ts
humanEscalationConditions: The installed CapCut version cannot render the generated validated MP4 visual clips.
The current FFmpeg or pycapcut installation lacks the required codec or animation support.
Existing dirty changes make a bounded edit unsafe.
